# Creating a signed token (signClick)

> Encodes click claims (impression ID and related data) as base64url JSON and appends a truncated HMAC-SHA256 signature.

_Part of [Signed click token with 30-minute expiry](click-token.md)_

When an ad is clicked, we create a signed token to prevent forged credits. The [`signClick`](ad-click-tracking-and-fraud.md) function takes a [`ClickClaims`](ad-click-tracking-and-fraud.md) object (with the impression ID—each impression can bill at most once—plus related fields) and a secret, encodes the claims as base64url JSON, signs it with HMAC-SHA256, and returns `payload.mac` (signature truncated to 32 base64url characters for brevity). Later, [`verifyClick`](ad-click-tracking-and-fraud.md) recomputes the signature to prove the token is authentic and not expired, as part of the [Ad click tokens and fraud checks](ad-click-tracking-and-fraud.md) verification.

**Look at:** [`signClick` in click-token.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/domain/click-token.ts#L17)

## Watch out

- The HMAC-SHA256 signature is truncated to 32 base64url characters, not the full digest—a space optimization.
- The secret must match exactly between [`signClick`](ad-click-tracking-and-fraud.md) and {{verify-click}}; different secrets cause verification to fail.
- The expiry time is encoded in the token itself, so old tokens are rejected without needing a database.
- Base64url encoding (not standard base64) makes the token safe for URLs without percent-escaping.
